verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              ततो निवेशाय तदा स विप्रः संशितव्रतः। महीं चचार दारार्थी न च दारानविन्दत॥१॥
verses.english: Sauti said : The Brahmana of hard austerities (Jaratkaru) roamed over the world for a wife, but he did not get a wife.

verses.sanskrit: स कदाचिद्वनं गत्वा विप्रः पितृवचः स्मरन्। चुक्रोश कन्याभिक्षार्थी तिस्रो वाचः शनैरिव॥२॥
verses.english: One day he went into the forest and remembering the words of his ancestors, he thrice begged for a bride in a faint voice.
verses.bhavadeepa: चतुर्दशः अध्यायः तत इति निवेशाय दारसङ्ग्रहाय पाठान्तरे यतिर्ब्रह्मचारी ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: तं वासुकिः प्रत्यगृह्णादुद्यम्य भगिनीं तदा। न स तां प्रतिजग्राह न सनाम्नीति चिन्तयन्॥३॥
verses.english: Thereupon, Vasuki appeared and offered his sister for the Rishi's acceptance. But the Rishi hesitated to accept her, thinking her to be not of the same name with himself.

verses.sanskrit: सनाम्नीं चोद्यतां भार्यां गृह्णीयामिति तस्य हि। मनो निविष्टमभवज्जरत्कारोर्महात्मनः॥४॥
verses.english: The high-souled Jaratkaru thought within himself, “I will take none for my wife who does not bear my name."

verses.sanskrit: तमुवाच महाप्राज्ञो जरत्कारुर्महातपाः। किं नाम्नी भगिनीयं ते ब्रूहि सत्यं भुजंगम॥५॥
verses.english: Then Jaratkaru, the great ascetic of rigid austerities, said, “O snake tell me truly what is the name of your sister?”

verses.sanskrit:
वासुकिरुवाच।
              जरत्कारो जरत्कारुः स्वसेयमनुजा मम। प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भार्यार्थे मया दत्तां सुमध्यमाम्। त्वदर्थं रक्षिता पूर्वं प्रतीच्छेमां द्विजोत्तम॥६॥
verses.english: Vasuki said: O Jaratkaru, my sister's name is also Jaratkaru. Given as a gift by me, accept this girl of slender waist for your wife. O best of the twice born, I had kept her in reserve for you. Therefore, take her.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा ततः प्रादाद्भार्यार्थे वरवर्णिनीम्। स च तां प्रतिजग्राह विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥७॥
verses.english: Saying this he offered his beautiful sister to Jaratkaru, who then married her according to the ordained rites.
